question.text: A cache access requires one clock cycle and handling cache miss stalls the processor for an additional 4 clock cycles. Which of the following cache hit rates comes closest to achieve an average memory access of 2 cycles?

answer.explanation: Average access time = 2. Cache access time = 1. Time to handle miss = 5. Let cache hit rate = $x$. $2=1\times x+5(1-x)$. $\Rightarrow x+5-5x=2$. $\Rightarrow -4x=-3$. $\Rightarrow x=\frac{3}{4}=0.75$. ∴ Hit ratio = 75%. Choice (A)

question.text: Consider a byte-addressable system with 16-bit addresses associated a cache, which has a two-way set-associative write-back cache with perfect LRU replacement. The Tag store requires a total of 4608 bits of storage. What is the block size of the cache?

answer.explanation: In 2-way set-associative cache, $t$(Tag) + $s$(Set) + $w$(Word) = 16$. For LRU, use 1-bit per set. For Valid bit, Dirty bit use 1 bit per block for each. Let tag has $t$-bits per block. Number of sets = $2^s$. Number of blocks = $2\times2^s$. Tag store size = $2^s+2\times2^s(2+t)$. Given tag store size = 4608 bits. $2^s+4\times2^s+2^{s+1}t=4608$. $\Rightarrow 5\times2^s+t\times2^{s+1}=2^{12}+2^9$. $\Rightarrow 2^s(2t+5)=2^9\times9$. $\Rightarrow s=9,t=2\Rightarrow w=5$. ∴ Block size = $2^5=32$ bytes. Choice (C)

Common Data for Questions 34 and 35: A processor requires 2000 cycles to perform a context switch and start an interrupt handler or 1000 cycles to poll an I/O device. An I/O device attached to that processor makes 100 requests per second, each of which takes 10,000 cycles to resolve once the handler has been started. By default, the processor polls every 0.5 ms if it is not using interrupts.
question.text: How many cycles per second does the CPU spend handling I/O from the device if interrupts are used?

answer.explanation: I/O device generates 100 requests. Each request requires an interrupt. The time taken for one request is = 2000 + 10000 + 2000 = 14000 (to start handler, execute handler, switch to original program). Total there are 100 requests so cycles required = 14000 × 100 = 1400000. Choice (A)

Common Data for Questions 34 and 35: A processor requires 2000 cycles to perform a context switch and start an interrupt handler or 1000 cycles to poll an I/O device. An I/O device attached to that processor makes 100 requests per second, each of which takes 10,000 cycles to resolve once the handler has been started. By default, the processor polls every 0.5 ms if it is not using interrupts.
question.text: How many cycles per second are spent on I/O if polling is used?

answer.explanation: The processor polls for every 0.5 ms. In one second there will be $\frac{1}{0.5\times10^{-3}}$ polls i.e., 2000 times. Each poll requires 1000 cycles. So it requires 2000000 cycles. There are 100 requests, each requires 10000 cycles, total 1000000 cycles to complete. ∴ Total time spent on I/O each second = 2000000 + 1000000 = 3000000. Choice (C)
